family_history: No relevant neurological or autoimmune family history

patient.chief_complaint: Confusion, seizures, and 'strange movements of the face' for 2 weeks
patient.history_present_illness: A 21-year-old right-handed woman with PCOS was brought by ambulance to the emergency department after being found by her dormitory roommates having a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. Her roommates report that she had been progressively deteriorating over the preceding 2 weeks. The illness began approximately 3 weeks ago with a febrile illness (documented temperature of 38.8 by thermometer) lasting about 5 days with headache, sore throat, and muscle aches. After apparent recovery from this febrile illness, she began developing insomnia and increasingly erratic behavior — sending bizarre text messages to family, laughing without apparent cause, and on one occasion accusing her roommates of 'switching her shampoo bottles to poison her.' Her parents were contacted and noted she 'wasn't herself' on video calls. She was evaluated by the student health clinic one week ago where a urine drug screen was negative and she was noted to have no fever; the assessment was 'possible stress reaction, query delusional disorder' and she was referred to university counseling services. Over the five days before today's admission, her roommates observed repetitive facial movements — constant grimacing, repetitive chewing, and what one roommate (a pre-med student) recognized as 'dyskinesias.' She had one brief unresponsive spell with arm stiffening three days prior. Today she had a 90-second GTCS and was brought by ambulance. She is not pregnant (LMP 2 weeks ago, COC compliant).

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but severely confused. Non-oriented. Periods of echolalia — repeating last words spoken by examiner. Continuous orofacial dyskinesias including lip-smacking, tongue protrusion, and repetitive jaw movements. Intermittent agitation.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 4mm bilaterally, reactive. Continuous perioral involuntary movements. Extraocular movements preserved.
neurological_exam.motor: Distal choreoathetosis bilateral upper extremities. Full strength on brief exam. Bilateral upper extremity posturing observed intermittently.
neurological_exam.additional: Autonomic instability: HR 126, BP fluctuating (118/70 to 158/94 during examination), temperature 37.9, diaphoresis. No meningismus.

Failing to perform pelvic imaging in young woman with limbic encephalitis
key_reasoning_points: PCOS history is coincidental — teratoma can occur on background of PCOS ovaries but is not caused by PCOS
Classic anti-NMDAR encephalitis presentation in young woman with febrile prodrome
EDB on EEG allows pre-antibody-result clinical diagnosis
Large teratoma (4.8 cm) requires urgent surgical management

red_herrings.intended_effect: May cause clinician to attribute ovarian findings to PCOS morphology and miss teratoma
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: PCOS and teratoma are independent conditions; ultrasound identifies a discrete complex mass consistent with dermoid cyst, not merely polycystic morphology

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Classic straightforward anti-NMDAR encephalitis in 21-year-old with PCOS — PCOS is a minor red herring for ovarian imaging interpretation.
